brewer_rules.label: Washed · light, floral/bright
brewer_rules.why: Clarity is the point — a fast cone lifts the florals and citrus. A French press would mute exactly what makes it special.

brewer_rules.label: Natural · fruit-forward
brewer_rules.why: The even, slower bed builds sweetness and body to carry the fruit; a fast V60 runs thin and channels on dense naturals.

brewer_rules.label: Honey · syrupy, sweet
brewer_rules.why: Immersion-then-drain squeezes out the syrupy honey sweetness and round mouthfeel without leaving silt in the cup.

brewer_rules.label: Anaerobic / experimental ferment
brewer_rules.why: High-intensity, boozy lots need taming, not amplifying. AeroPress gives control over contact time and temperature.

brewer_rules.label: Dark roast · chocolatey, for milk
brewer_rules.brewer: Moka pot, AeroPress or S. Indian filter
brewer_rules.why: Pressure/percolation suits roast depth and body, and stands up to milk. A fast V60 goes flat and ashy on dark roasts.

brewer_rules.label: Dense natural / robusta · body-forward
brewer_rules.why: Body is the goal here — embrace the oils and texture instead of filtering them out. A cone would strip the best part.
